intended_object: For a vector v ∈ V, the k-algebra homomorphism Sym(V*) → k[t] that restricts a polynomial function on V to the line through v, f ↦ (t ↦ f(t·v)). It is the comorphism of the cone line 𝔸¹ → V, t ↦ t v, and is determined by φ ↦ φ(v)·t on linear forms. This reading comes from the docstring ("cone-line map"), the module documentation and how the file uses the map: its kernel is the homogeneous ideal of the point [v].
explanation:
The body is `SymmetricAlgebra.lift` applied to the linear map φ ↦ C(φ v)·X. By the universal property of the symmetric algebra, this is the unique k-algebra map Sym(V*) → k[t] that sends each linear form φ to φ(v)·t. A product of linear forms φ₁⋯φ_d therefore goes to (∏ φᵢ(v))·t^d, which is exactly evaluation along t ↦ t v. The map is graded, so its kernel is the homogeneous ideal of polynomials vanishing on the line k·v. That ideal is the vanishing ideal of the point [v] ∈ ℙ(V) when v ≠ 0, and that is how the file uses it (`symmetricAlgebraHomogeneousCoordinateIdeal`, and the comparison with the basis-dependent `homogeneousCoordinateMap`).

There are no degenerate-case problems. For v = 0 the map sends every positive-degree element to 0, which is correct; the library only builds points under the hypothesis v ≠ 0.

The same construction would work over any commutative ring. Here, however, it is an auxiliary map inside a development of projective space over a field, and the downstream results need a field anyway (closed points, algebraically closed k). So restricting to `[Field k]` is not a meaningful narrowing. Mathlib has no ready-made named declaration for this cone-line evaluation map on `SymmetricAlgebra`.
